cls: Hepatitis B immune globulin (passive immunizing agent)
pharm: Provides passive immunity by supplying preformed human antibodies to hepatitis B surface antigen (anti-HBs), reducing the attack rate of hepatitis B after exposure.
quick: Percutaneous/sexual exposure 0.06 mL/kg IM; give with HB vaccine
Category C; use only if clearly indicated
Excretion in milk unknown; use with caution
No specific dose adjustment (IM, not renally limited)
Injection-site/hypersensitivity reactions; defer live vaccines ~3 months
summary: Human Hepatitis B Immunoglobulin (Nabi-HB) is a plasma-derived sterile solution of immunoglobulin rich in antibodies to hepatitis B surface antigen (anti-HBs). It provides immediate, temporary passive protection after exposure to HBV and is given intramuscularly only (never IV). It is indicated for acute (percutaneous, mucous membrane, or oral) exposure to HBsAg-positive blood, perinatal exposure of infants born to HBsAg-positive mothers, sexual exposure to HBsAg-positive persons, and certain household exposures. For greatest effect it is given as soon as possible after exposure and, when indicated, together with (but at a separate site from) hepatitis B vaccine. It is generally well tolerated, with mostly mild local and systemic reactions; rare anaphylaxis can occur, especially in IgA-deficient individuals.
indications: Acute exposure to blood containing HBsAg (needlestick, bite, sharps, mucous membrane splash, or oral/pipetting accident)
Perinatal exposure of infants born to HBsAg-positive mothers (with or without HBeAg)
Household exposure to persons with acute HBV infection (infants <12 months whose mother/primary caregiver is HBsAg-positive; other contacts with identifiable blood exposure)

dosage.t: Single dose as soon as possible after exposure, within 24 hours if possible
dosage.n: Begin HB vaccine series; value uncertain after 7 days. Non-responders/vaccine-refusers: repeat dose 1 month later

dosage.c: Perinatal exposure - infant of HBsAg-positive mother
dosage.t: After physiologic stabilization, preferably within 12 hours of birth
dosage.n: Start HB vaccine series simultaneously, first dose concurrently but at a different site

dosage.c: Perinatal - mother not screened, later found HBsAg-positive
dosage.t: As soon as possible, no later than 7 days after birth
dosage.n: Efficacy after 48 hours of age is not known; give HB vaccine within 12 hours of birth

dosage.t: Single dose within 14 days of last sexual contact
dosage.n: Begin HB vaccine series; combination may improve efficacy

admin: For intramuscular use ONLY - do not administer intravenously
Preferred injection sites: anterolateral upper thigh or deltoid muscle
If buttock is used, use only the upper outer quadrant and direct the needle anteriorly to avoid the sciatic nerve
Inspect for particulate matter and discoloration before use; product is clear to opalescent
Use a separate vial, sterile syringe, and needle for each patient to prevent transmission of infectious agents
Contains no preservative; use any entered vial promptly (within 6 hours) and discard partially used vials
Do not mix with other drugs; may give same day as HB vaccine but at a different site
Give as soon as possible after exposure for greatest effectiveness
moa: Hepatitis B Immune Globulin (Human) provides passive immunization by delivering high titers of preformed human antibodies to hepatitis B surface antigen (anti-HBs). These antibodies bind and neutralize circulating HBV, preventing establishment of infection or limiting its spread after exposure, as evidenced by a reduced attack rate of hepatitis B. When given with hepatitis B vaccine, it provides immediate passive protection while the vaccine elicits active, long-lasting immunity; the combination is most effective for neonatal and high-risk exposures.

absolute: Prior anaphylactic or severe systemic reaction to human immune globulin or human globulin
relative: IgA deficiency (potential to form anti-IgA antibodies and develop anaphylactic reactions; product contains up to 40 mcg/mL IgA)
Severe thrombocytopenia or any coagulation disorder that contraindicates IM injection (give only if benefit outweighs risk)
monitor: Hypersensitivity/anaphylactic reactions during and after administration
Coagulation status before IM injection in at-risk patients

preg: Pregnancy Category C. Animal reproduction studies have not been conducted. It is not known whether the product can cause fetal harm or affect reproductive capacity; give to a pregnant woman only if clearly indicated.
lact: It is not known whether the product is excreted in human milk. Because many drugs are excreted in human milk, exercise caution when administering to a nursing mother.
renal: No specific renal dose adjustment is described; the product is given intramuscularly and is not eliminated by renal mechanisms in a clinically significant dose-limiting way.
hepatic: No specific hepatic dose adjustment is described in the label.

major: Live virus vaccines (e.g., measles, mumps, rubella, varicella) - may blunt response; defer live vaccination until ~3 months after this product, and revaccination may be needed if given shortly after live vaccine
moderate: Hepatitis B vaccine - may be given at the same time (different site) or up to one month before vaccination without impairing the active immune response (intended combination, not an adverse interaction)
interactions.diagnostics: Passively transferred antibodies may transiently affect some serologic test results; mild transient elevations in alkaline phosphatase, AST, and creatinine were reported in trials.

rare: Transient elevated alkaline phosphatase/AST or creatinine
emergency: Anaphylaxis (rare, reported with human immune globulins) - have epinephrine and supportive measures available

monitoring: Observe for hypersensitivity/anaphylactic reactions after injection
For perinatal cases, test infant for HBsAg and anti-HBs at 12-15 months of age
Defer live virus vaccines for ~3 months after administration
counsel: This medicine gives immediate, temporary protection against hepatitis B after an exposure
It is given as a shot into the muscle and must not be given into a vein
It works best when given as soon as possible after exposure
You will usually also need the hepatitis B vaccine series for long-lasting protection
Tell your provider if you have ever had a severe reaction to immune globulin or are IgA deficient
Avoid live virus vaccines for about 3 months after this injection unless your provider advises otherwise
Mild soreness, redness at the injection site, headache, or muscle aches may occur
pk: Immediate passive protection after IM administration
Maximum concentration reached at ~6.5 days (range ~6.5 +/- 4.3 days)
Temporary protection over weeks; second dose at 1 month for non-responders
Refrigerate at 2 to 8 C (36 to 46 F); do not freeze; use within 6 hours after vial is entered
pearls: Intramuscular use ONLY - never give Nabi-HB intravenously
Perinatal dose is 0.5 mL IM within 12 hours of birth; exposure dose is 0.06 mL/kg IM
Give as soon as possible after exposure - value is unclear after 7 days
Should be given WITH hepatitis B vaccine when indicated (different site) - combination is 85-98% effective in preventing the neonatal carrier state
Plasma-derived; despite solvent/detergent and nanofiltration viral-reduction steps, theoretical infection risk remains
Use caution in IgA-deficient patients (risk of anaphylaxis); defer live virus vaccines ~3 months
missed: Not a scheduled maintenance medication. Effectiveness depends on prompt administration after exposure - give as soon as possible (within hours to a few days). For non-responders or vaccine-refusers after acute exposure, a second dose is given one month after the first.
overdose: No overdose data are available; clinical experience with other human immune globulins suggests the only manifestations would be pain and tenderness at the injection site. Manage with local supportive care.
